cond_0001.intro:
We are seeking an AWS Certified Weld Inspector (CWI) to support our structural steel fabrication and highway component/railings division.
Certified Welding Inspectors use their knowledge of welding processes, test methods, discontinuities, materials, qualifications, and standards to ensure that weldments and welding-related activities comply with all applicable quality and safety criteria.
The role of the CWI is critical to the safety and structural soundness of the vast number of buildings, vehicles, machinery, and consumer products that require strong, secure welds.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to execute each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. This list is not all inclusive of the role's potential requirements.
Key Performance Objectives (not an all-inclusive list of duties/expectations)
Read plans and write reports complying with code specs.
Ensure that all materials specified on the shop drawings and TxDOT form 1818 are used during fabrication and accurate traceability of the material through fabrication.
Ensure use of proper WPSs and properly certified welding personnel.
Perform visual inspection on welded products, structures in progress, and systems to assess their quality, workmanship, and compliance with relevant codes, standards, and specifications.
Perform inspections both in house and at vendor locations as needed.
Maintain accurate records of inspection activities, including reports on weld quality, non-conformities, and corrective actions. Ensure all documentation complies with relevant regulations.
Prepare detailed inspection reports, including photographs, drawings, and other relevant documentation as needed.
Collaborate with the quality control team to ensure welding procedures are followed and fabricated products meet required quality standards.
Verify proper weld joint preparation, fit up, and evaluation of the welds to the requirements of AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code - Steel or the AWS D1.2 Structural Welding Code - Aluminum.
Use WPS or PQR sample forms located in the current applicable AWS code or approved equal.
Verify that repairs are made using the required repair procedure and any required NDT is completed on the repair.
Conduct and stamp final acceptance of the product.
Assist with the coordination of the annual AISC internal audit.
Stay updated on industry codes and standards (AISC) and ensure welding processes adhere to these specifications.
Ensure adherence to safety protocols and practices during welding operations.
Stay current with certifications and pursue additional training as necessary to maintain Certified Welding Inspector status.
Provide guidance and training to welding personnel when needed.
Investigate and analyze welding-related issues, identify root causes, and recommend corrective actions to address any deficiencies.
Attention to detail.
Key Competencies
Must be able to read a tape measure.
Comply with Health and Safety, Environmental and company manufacturing policies and procedures.
Maintain a positive work atmosphere by communicating effectively with co-workers, clients, quality control, and supervisors.
Perform daily cleaning and maintenance of area.
Work in a safe and conscientious manner.
Lift 50+ pounds.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Current Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification.
AWS D1.1 Credentials.
Minimum of 2 years of experience in welding inspection within the steel fabrication and metal railings industry.
Knowledge of welding inspection and related NDE methods (MT, PT, UT, and RT), including ASME Sec. V requirements.
Proficient working knowledge (welder) and understanding of welding processes, including SMAW, GMAW, GTAW, and FCAW.
Familiarity with welding codes and standards such as AWS, ASME, and API.
Good verbal and written communication skills, including knowledge of AWS A3.0 Welding Terms and Definitions.
Strong coordination and organization skills, with strict emphasis on accuracy and attention to detail.
Ability to communicate effectively, both verbal and written, with all internal organization departments, suppliers, subcontractors, and regulatory authorities.
Meticulous attention to detail in inspections and documentation.
Ability to analyze problems and implement effective solutions.
Must pass a drug test and background check.
Clean driving record.
Preferred Requirements
TxDOT industry experience.
Understanding of specifications relevant to TxDOT requirements.
Experience with AISC certification.
Familiarity with coatings for steel - galvanized, painting, powder coating.
Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to analyze complex welding-related issues and fixture design challenges.
Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.

cond_0094.intro:
We are seeking an AWS Certified Weld Inspector (CWI) to support our structural steel fabrication and highway component/railings division. Certified Welding Inspectors employ their extensive knowledge of welding processes, test methods, discontinuities, materials, qualifications, and standards to ensure that weldments and welding-related activities comply with all applicable quality and safety criteria.
The role of the CWI is critical to the safety and structural soundness of the vast number of buildings, vehicles, machinery, and consumer products that require strong, secure welds. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of welding codes, inspection standards, and fabrication requirements.
cond_0094.responsibilities:
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to execute each essential duty satisfactorily if not above expectations. The requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. This list is not all inclusive of the role's potential requirements.
Key Performance Objectives (not an all-inclusive list of duties/expectations)
Able to read plans and write reports complying with code specs. Ensure that all Materials specified on the shop drawings and TxDOT form 1818 are used during fabrication and accurate traceability of the material through fabrication. Ensure use of proper WPSs and properly certified welding personnel. Perform Visual inspection on welded products, structures in progress, and systems to assess their quality, workmanship, and compliance with relevant codes, standards, and specifications. Performs inspections both in house and at vendor locations as needed. Maintain accurate records of inspection activities, including reports on weld quality, non-conformities, and corrective actions. Ensure all documentation complies with relevant regulations. Prepare detailed inspection reports, including photographs, drawings, and other relevant documentation as needed. Collaborate with the quality control team to ensure welding procedures are followed and fabricated products meet required quality standards. CWI verifies proper weld joint preparation, fit up, and evaluation of the welds to the requirements of AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code - Steel or the AWS D1.2 Structural Welding Code - Aluminum. Use WPS or PQR sample forms located in the current applicable AWS code or approved equal. Verification that repairs are made using the required repair procedure and any required NDT is completed on the repair. Final acceptance of the product is conducted and stamped by the CWI. Assist with the coordination of the annual AISC internal audit. Stay updated on industry codes and standards (AISC) and ensure welding processes adhere to these specifications. Ensure adherence to safety protocols and practices during welding operations. Stay current with certifications and pursue additional training as necessary to maintain Certified Welding Inspector status. Provide guidance and training to welding personnel when needed. Investigate and analyze welding-related issues, identify root causes, and recommend corrective actions to address any deficiencies. Attention to details.
Key Competencies
MUST BE ABLE TO READ A TAPE MEASURE. Comply with Health and Safety, Environmental and company's manufacturing policies, and procedures. Maintains positive work atmosphere by functioning and communicating in an effective manner with co-workers, clients, quality control, and supervisors. Performs daily cleaning and maintenance of area. Works in a safe and conscientious manner. Lift 50+ pounds.

Certified Welding Inspectors employ their extensive knowledge of welding processes, test methods, discontinuities, materials, qualifications, and standards to ensure that weldments and welding-related activities comply with all applicable quality and safety criteria.
The role of the CWI is critical to the safety and structural soundness of the vast number of buildings, vehicles, machinery, and consumer products that require strong, secure welds.
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to execute each essential duty satisfactorily if not above expectations. The requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and / or ability required. This list is not all inclusive of the role's potential requirements.
Key Performance Objectives (not an all-inclusive list of duties/expectations)
Able to read plans and write reports complying with code specs. Ensure that all Materials specified on the shop drawings and TxDOT form 1818 are used during fabrication and accurate traceability of the material through fabrication. Ensure use of proper WPSs and properly certified welding personnel. Perform Visual inspection on welded products, structures in progress, and systems to assess their quality, workmanship, and compliance with relevant codes, standards, and specifications. Performs inspections both in house and at vendor locations as needed. Maintain accurate records of inspection activities, including reports on weld quality, non-conformities, and corrective actions. Ensure all documentation complies with relevant regulations. Prepare detailed inspection reports, including photographs, drawings, and other relevant documentation as needed. Collaborate with the quality control team to ensure welding procedures are followed and fabricated products meet required quality standards. CWI verifies proper weld joint preparation, fit up, and evaluation of the welds to the requirements of AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code - Steel or the AWS D1.2 Structural Welding Code - Aluminum. Use WPS or PQR sample forms located in the current applicable AWS code or approved equal. Verification that repairs are made using the required repair procedure and any required NDT is completed on the repair. Final acceptance of the product is conducted and stamped by the CWI. Assist with the coordination of the annual AISC internal audit. Stay updated on industry codes and standards (AISC) and ensure welding processes adhere to these specifications. Ensure adherence to safety protocols and practices during welding operations. Stay current with certifications and pursue additional training as necessary to maintain Certified Welding Inspector status. Provide guidance and training to welding personnel when needed. Investigate and analyze welding-related issues, identify root causes, and recommend corrective actions to address any deficiencies. Attention to details.
Key Competencies
MUST BE ABLE TO READ A TAPE MEASURE. Comply with Health and Safety, Environmental and company's manufacturing policies, and procedures. Maintains positive work atmosphere by functioning and communicating in an effective manner with co-workers, clients, quality control, and supervisors. Performs daily cleaning and maintenance of area. Works in a safe and conscientious manner. Lift 50+ pounds.
This Job Is Ideal For Someone Who Is
Dependable -- more reliable than spontaneous. Adaptable/flexible -- enjoys doing work that requires frequent shifts in direction. Achievement-oriented -- enjoys taking on challenges, even if they might fail. Autonomous/Independent -- enjoys working with little direction. High stress tolerance -- thrives in a high-pressure environment.
cond_0101.requirements: Current Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification is required. Must have AWS D1.1 Credentials. Minimum of 2 years of demonstrated expertise in welding inspection within the steel fabrication and metal railings industry. TxDOT industry a plus. Advanced knowledge of specifications relevant to TxDOT requirements. Proven track record with AISC certification. Solid understanding of coatings for steel - galvanized, painting, powder coating. Exceptional communication skills, both verbal and written, with all internal organization departments, suppliers, subcontractors, and regulatory authorities. Strong coordination and organization skills, with strict emphasis on accuracy and attention to detail. Strong verbal and written communication skills, including deep knowledge of AWS A3.0 Welding Terms and Definitions. Advanced knowledge of welding inspection and related NDE methods (MT, PT, UT, and RT), including ASME Sec. V requirements. Strong command of welding processes, including SMAW, GMAW, GTAW, and FCAW. Expertise in welding codes and standards such as AWS, ASME, and API. Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to analyze complex welding-related issues and fixture design challenges. Meticulous attention to detail in inspections and documentation. Proven ability to analyze problems and implement effective solutions. Strong leadership abilities to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams. Must pass a drug test and background check. Clean driving records.

cond_0176.intro: We are seeking an AWS Certified Weld Inspector (CWI) to support our structural steel fabrication and highway component/railings division. This position offers high-visibility and growth opportunities. Certified Welding Inspectors employ their extensive knowledge of welding processes, test methods, discontinuities, materials, qualifications, and standards to ensure that weldments and welding-related activities comply with all applicable quality and safety criteria. The role of the CWI is critical to the safety and structural soundness of the vast number of buildings, vehicles, machinery, and consumer products that require strong, secure welds. People usually grow into this role over time as they build experience with welding inspection and fabrication work.
cond_0176.responsibilities:
Able to read plans and write reports complying with code specs.
Ensure that all Materials specified on the shop drawings and TxDOT form 1818 are used during fabrication and accurate traceability of the material through fabrication.
Ensure use of proper WPSs and properly certified welding personnel.
Perform Visual inspection on welded products, structures in progress, and systems to assess their quality, workmanship, and compliance with relevant codes, standards, and specifications.
Performs inspections both in house and at vendor locations as needed.
Maintain accurate records of inspection activities, including reports on weld quality, non-conformities, and corrective actions.
Ensure all documentation complies with relevant regulations.
Prepare detailed inspection reports, including photographs, drawings, and other relevant documentation as needed.
Collaborate with the quality control team to ensure welding procedures are followed and fabricated products meet required quality standards.
CWI verifies proper weld joint preparation, fit up, and evaluation of the welds to the requirements of AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code - Steel or the AWS D1.2 Structural Welding Code - Aluminum.
Use WPS or PQR sample forms located in the current applicable AWS code or approved equal.
Verification that repairs are made using the required repair procedure and any required NDT is completed on the repair.
Final acceptance of the product is conducted and stamped by the CWI.
Assist with the coordination of the annual AISC internal audit.
Stay updated on industry codes and standards (AISC) and ensure welding processes adhere to these specifications.
Ensure adherence to safety protocols and practices during welding operations.
Stay current with certifications and pursue additional training as necessary to maintain Certified Welding Inspector status.
Provide guidance and training to welding personnel when needed.
Investigate and analyze welding-related issues, identify root causes, and recommend corrective actions to address any deficiencies.
Attention to details.

Ensure adherence to safety protocols and practices during welding operations.

Provide guidance and training to welding personnel when needed, explaining requirements clearly and handling questions directly.

cond_0226.intro:
We are seeking a AWS Certified Weld Inspector (CWI) to support our structural steel fabrication and highway component/railings division. This position offers high-visibility, growth opportunities, and exciting builds.
Certified Welding Inspectors employ their extensive knowledge of welding processes, test methods, discontinuities, materials, qualifications, and standards to ensure that weldments and welding-related activities comply with all applicable quality and safety criteria.
The role of the CWI is critical to the safety and structural soundness of the vast number of buildings, vehicles, machinery, and consumer products that require strong, secure welds.
cond_0226.responsibilities:
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to execute each essential duty satisfactorily if not above expectations. The requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and / or ability required. This list is not all inclusive of the role's potential requirements.
Key Performance Objectives (not an all-inclusive list of duties/expectations)
Able to read plans and write reports complying with code specs. Ensure that all Materials specified on the shop drawings and TxDOT form 1818 are used during fabrication and accurate traceability of the material through fabrication. Ensure use of proper WPSs and properly certified welding personnel. Perform Visual inspection on welded products, structures in progress, and systems to assess their quality, workmanship, and compliance with relevant codes, standards, and specifications. Performs inspections both in house and at vendor locations as needed. Maintain accurate records of inspection activities, including reports on weld quality, non-conformities, and corrective actions. Ensure all documentation complies with relevant regulations. Prepare detailed inspection reports, including photographs, drawings, and other relevant documentation as needed. Collaborate with the quality control team to ensure welding procedures are followed and fabricated products meet required quality standards. CWI verifies proper weld joint preparation, fit up, and evaluation of the welds to the requirements of AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code - Steel or the AWS D1.2 Structural Welding Code - Aluminum. Use WPS or PQR sample forms located in the current applicable AWS code or approved equal. Verification that repairs are made using the required repair procedure and any required NDT is completed on the repair. Final acceptance of the product is conducted and stamped by the CWI. Assist with the coordination of the annual AISC internal audit. Stay updated on industry codes and standards (AISC) and ensure welding processes adhere to these specifications. Ensure adherence to safety protocols and practices during welding operations. Stay current with certifications and pursue additional training as necessary to maintain Certified Welding Inspector status. Provide guidance and training to welding personnel when needed. Investigate and analyze welding-related issues, identify root causes, and recommend corrective actions to address any deficiencies. Attention to details.
Key Competencies
MUST BE ABLE TO READ A TAPE MEASURE. Comply with Health and Safety, Environmental and company's manufacturing policies, and procedures. Maintains positive work atmosphere by functioning and communicating in an effective manner with co-workers, clients, quality control, and supervisors. Performs daily cleaning and maintenance of area. Works in a safe and conscientious manner. Lift 50+ pounds.
cond_0226.requirements:
Current Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification is required. Must have AWS D1.1 Credentials. Minimum of 2 years of experience in welding inspection within the steel fabrication and metal railings industry. TxDOT industry a plus. Understanding of specifications relevant to TXDOT requirements. Experience with AISC certification. Familiar with coatings for steel - galvanized, painting, powder coating. Ability to communicate effectively, both verbal and written, with all internal organization departments, suppliers, subcontractors, and regulatory authorities. Strong coordination and organization skills, with strict emphasis on accuracy and attention to detail. Good verbal and written communication skills, including knowledge of AWS A3.0 Welding Terms and Definitions. Knowledge of welding inspection and related NDE methods (MT, PT, UT, and RT), including ASME Sec. V requirements. Proficient working knowledge (welder) and understanding of welding processes, including SMAW, GMAW, GTAW, and FCAW. Familiarity with welding codes and standards such as AWS, ASME, and API. Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to analyze complex welding-related issues and fixture design challenges. Meticulous attention to detail in inspections and documentation. Proven ability to analyze problems and implement effective solutions. Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams. Must pass a drug test and background check. Clean driving records.
This Job Is Ideal For Someone Who Is
Dependable -- more reliable than spontaneous. Adaptable/flexible -- enjoys doing work that requires frequent shifts in direction. Achievement-oriented -- enjoys taking on challenges, even if they might fail. Autonomous/Independent -- enjoys working with little direction. High stress tolerance -- thrives in a high-pressure environment.

We are looking for an AWS Certified Weld Inspector (CWI) to join our structural steel fabrication and highway component/railings division.
Certified Welding Inspectors apply their knowledge of welding processes, test methods, discontinuities, materials, qualifications, and standards to ensure that weldments and welding-related activities comply with all applicable quality and safety criteria.
The CWI is critical to the safety and structural soundness of buildings, vehicles, machinery, and consumer products that require strong, secure welds.
cond_0278.responsibilities:
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to execute each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. This list is not all-inclusive.
Read plans and write reports complying with code specs.
Ensure all materials specified on shop drawings and TxDOT form 1818 are used during fabrication and maintain accurate material traceability through fabrication.
Ensure use of proper WPSs and properly certified welding personnel.
Execute visual inspections on welded products, structures in progress, and systems to assess quality, workmanship, and compliance with relevant codes, standards, and specifications.
Conduct inspections both in-house and at vendor locations as needed.
Maintain accurate records of inspection activities, including reports on weld quality, non-conformities, and corrective actions; ensure all documentation complies with relevant regulations.
Produce detailed inspection reports, including photographs, drawings, and other relevant documentation as needed.
Work with the quality control team to ensure welding procedures are followed and fabricated products meet required quality standards.
Verify proper weld joint preparation, fit-up, and evaluation of welds to the requirements of AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code - Steel or AWS D1.2 Structural Welding Code - Aluminum.
Use WPS or PQR sample forms located in the current applicable AWS code or approved equal.
Verify that repairs are made using the required repair procedure and that any required NDT is completed on the repair.
Conduct and stamp final acceptance of the product.
Lead coordination of the annual AISC internal audit.
Stay current on industry codes and standards (AISC) and ensure welding processes adhere to these specifications.
Enforce adherence to safety protocols and practices during welding operations.
Maintain certifications and pursue additional training as necessary to retain Certified Welding Inspector status.
Provide guidance and training to welding personnel when needed.
Investigate and analyze welding-related issues, determine root causes, and implement corrective actions to address deficiencies.
Maintain attention to detail throughout all tasks.
cond_0278.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Current Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification.
AWS D1.1 Credentials.
Minimum of 2 years of experience in welding inspection within the steel fabrication and metal railings industry.
Knowledge of welding inspection and related NDE methods (MT, PT, UT, and RT), including ASME Sec. V requirements.
Proficient working knowledge (welder) and understanding of welding processes, including SMAW, GMAW, GTAW, and FCAW.
Familiarity with welding codes and standards such as AWS, ASME, and API.
Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with internal departments, suppliers, subcontractors, and regulatory authorities.
Strong coordination and organization skills, with strict emphasis on accuracy and attention to detail.
Good verbal and written communication skills, including knowledge of AWS A3.0 Welding Terms and Definitions.
Must pass a drug test and background check.
Clean driving record.
Must be able to read a tape measure.
Comply with Health and Safety, Environmental, and company manufacturing policies and procedures.
Maintain a positive work atmosphere by communicating effectively with co-workers, clients, quality control, and supervisors.
Perform daily cleaning and maintenance of area.
Work in a safe and conscientious manner.
Able to lift 50+ pounds.
Preferred Requirements
TxDOT industry experience.
Understanding of specifications relevant to TxDOT requirements.
Experience with AISC certification.
Familiarity with coatings for steel — galvanized, painting, powder coating.
Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to analyze complex welding-related issues and fixture design challenges.
Meticulous attention to detail in inspections and documentation.
Proven ability to analyze problems and implement effective solutions.
Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.

Certified Welding Inspectors employ their extensive knowledge of welding processes, test methods, discontinuities, materials, qualifications, and standards to ensure that weldments and welding-related activities comply with all applicable quality and safety criteria.
The role of the CWI is critical to the safety and structural soundness of the vast number of buildings, vehicles, machinery, and consumer products that require strong, secure welds.
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to execute each essential duty satisfactorily if not above expectations. The requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. This list is not all inclusive of the role's potential requirements.
Key Performance Objectives (not an all-inclusive list of duties/expectations)
Able to read plans and write reports complying with code specs. Ensure that all Materials specified on the shop drawings and TxDOT form 1818 are used during fabrication and accurate traceability of the material through fabrication. Ensure use of proper WPSs and properly certified welding personnel. Perform Visual inspection on welded products, structures in progress, and systems to assess their quality, workmanship, and compliance with relevant codes, standards, and specifications. Performs inspections both in house and at vendor locations as needed. Maintain accurate records of inspection activities, including reports on weld quality, non-conformities, and corrective actions. Ensure all documentation complies with relevant regulations. Prepare detailed inspection reports, including photographs, drawings, and other relevant documentation as needed. Collaborate with the quality control team to ensure welding procedures are followed and fabricated products meet required quality standards. CWI verifies proper weld joint preparation, fit up, and evaluation of the welds to the requirements of AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code - Steel or the AWS D1.2 Structural Welding Code - Aluminum. Use WPS or PQR sample forms located in the current applicable AWS code or approved equal. Verification that repairs are made using the required repair procedure and any required NDT is completed on the repair. Final acceptance of the product is conducted and stamped by the CWI. Assist with the coordination of the annual AISC internal audit. Stay updated on industry codes and standards (AISC) and ensure welding processes adhere to these specifications. Ensure adherence to safety protocols and practices during welding operations. Stay current with certifications and pursue additional training as necessary to maintain Certified Welding Inspector status. Provide guidance and training to welding personnel when needed. Investigate and analyze welding-related issues, identify root causes, and recommend corrective actions to address any deficiencies. Attention to details.
Key Competencies
MUST BE ABLE TO READ A TAPE MEASURE. Comply with Health and Safety, Environmental and company's manufacturing policies, and procedures. Maintains positive work atmosphere by functioning and communicating in an effective manner with co-workers, clients, quality control, and supervisors. Performs daily cleaning and maintenance of area. Works in a safe and conscientious manner. Lift 50+ pounds.
cond_0291.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Current Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification with AWS D1.1 Credentials.
Around 2 years of experience in welding inspection within the steel fabrication and metal railings industry, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Working knowledge of welding inspection and related NDE methods (MT, PT, UT, and RT), including ASME Sec. V requirements.
Familiarity with welding processes, including SMAW, GMAW, GTAW, and FCAW.
Familiarity with welding codes and standards such as AWS, ASME, and API.
Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with internal departments, suppliers, subcontractors, and regulatory authorities.
Must pass a drug test and background check.
Clean driving record.
Preferred Requirements
Background in TxDOT industry and understanding of specifications relevant to TxDOT requirements.
Experience with AISC certification.
Familiarity with coatings for steel — galvanized, painting, powder coating.
Knowledge of AWS A3.0 Welding Terms and Definitions.
Ability to analyze welding-related issues and fixture design challenges.
Openness to collaborating with cross-functional teams and willingness to work through complex problems with others.
Good coordination and organizational habits, with attention to accuracy and detail.

The CWI is accountable for the safety and structural integrity of the products we build, from buildings and vehicles to machinery and consumer goods that depend on strong, secure welds.
cond_0305.responsibilities:
Execute each essential duty to a high standard. The list below is representative but not all-inclusive.
Read plans and write reports that comply with code specs. Ensure all materials specified on shop drawings and TxDOT form 1818 are used during fabrication and maintain accurate material traceability throughout. Enforce use of proper WPSs and verify that welding personnel hold current certifications. Conduct visual inspections on welded products, structures in progress, and systems to assess quality, workmanship, and compliance with relevant codes, standards, and specifications. Carry out inspections both in-house and at vendor locations as needed. Maintain accurate records of inspection activities, including reports on weld quality, non-conformities, and corrective actions, and ensure all documentation complies with relevant regulations. Produce detailed inspection reports, including photographs, drawings, and other relevant documentation. Lead coordination with the quality control team to ensure welding procedures are followed and fabricated products meet required quality standards. Verify proper weld joint preparation, fit-up, and weld evaluation against AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code - Steel or AWS D1.2 Structural Welding Code - Aluminum. Apply WPS or PQR sample forms from the current applicable AWS code or approved equal. Verify that repairs are completed using the required repair procedure and that any required NDT is performed on the repair. Conduct and stamp final product acceptance. Direct coordination of the annual AISC internal audit. Stay current on industry codes and standards (AISC) and ensure welding processes adhere to these specifications. Enforce adherence to safety protocols and practices during welding operations. Maintain CWI certification and pursue additional training as needed. Deliver guidance and training to welding personnel when needed. Investigate welding-related issues, determine root causes, and implement corrective actions to resolve deficiencies. Apply strict attention to detail throughout all activities.
cond_0305.requirements:
Current Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification is required. Must have AWS D1.1 Credentials. Minimum of 2 years of experience in welding inspection within the steel fabrication and metal railings industry. TxDOT industry experience a plus. Understanding of specifications relevant to TxDOT requirements. Experience with AISC certification. Familiar with coatings for steel - galvanized, painting, powder coating. Ability to communicate effectively, both verbal and written, with all internal organization departments, suppliers, subcontractors, and regulatory authorities. Strong coordination and organization skills, with strict emphasis on accuracy and attention to detail. Good verbal and written communication skills, including knowledge of AWS A3.0 Welding Terms and Definitions. Knowledge of welding inspection and related NDE methods (MT, PT, UT, and RT), including ASME Sec. V requirements. Proficient working knowledge (welder) and understanding of welding processes, including SMAW, GMAW, GTAW, and FCAW. Familiarity with welding codes and standards such as AWS, ASME, and API. Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to analyze complex welding-related issues and fixture design challenges. Meticulous attention to detail in inspections and documentation. Proven ability to analyze problems and implement effective solutions. Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams. Must pass a drug test and background check. Clean driving record.
MUST BE ABLE TO READ A TAPE MEASURE. Comply with Health and Safety, Environmental and company's manufacturing policies and procedures. Maintains positive work atmosphere by functioning and communicating in an effective manner with co-workers, clients, quality control, and supervisors. Performs daily cleaning and maintenance of area. Works in a safe and conscientious manner. Lift 50+ pounds.
Dependable -- more reliable than spontaneous. Adaptable/flexible -- enjoys doing work that requires frequent shifts in direction. Achievement-oriented -- enjoys taking on challenges, even if they might fail. Autonomous/Independent -- enjoys working with little direction. High stress tolerance -- thrives in a high-pressure environment.

We are looking for an AWS Certified Weld Inspector (CWI) to support our structural steel fabrication and highway component/railings division, working alongside our quality control and fabrication teams.
Certified Welding Inspectors apply their knowledge of welding processes, test methods, discontinuities, materials, qualifications, and standards to help ensure that weldments and welding-related activities comply with all applicable quality and safety criteria.
The CWI works closely with fabrication and quality teams to support the safety and structural soundness of buildings, vehicles, machinery, and consumer products that require strong, secure welds.
cond_0459.responsibilities: Read plans and write reports in compliance with code specs. Help ensure that all materials specified on shop drawings and TxDOT form 1818 are used during fabrication, and support accurate traceability of material through fabrication. Help ensure use of proper WPSs and properly certified welding personnel. Perform visual inspections on welded products, structures in progress, and systems to assess quality, workmanship, and compliance with relevant codes, standards, and specifications. Conduct inspections both in-house and at vendor locations as needed. Maintain accurate records of inspection activities, including reports on weld quality, non-conformities, and corrective actions, and help ensure all documentation complies with relevant regulations. Prepare detailed inspection reports, including photographs, drawings, and other relevant documentation as needed. Work with the quality control team to help ensure welding procedures are followed and fabricated products meet required quality standards. Verify proper weld joint preparation, fit-up, and evaluation of welds to the requirements of AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code - Steel or AWS D1.2 Structural Welding Code - Aluminum. Use WPS or PQR sample forms from the current applicable AWS code or approved equal. Verify that repairs are made using the required repair procedure and that any required NDT is completed on the repair. Conduct and stamp final acceptance of the product. Assist with coordination of the annual AISC internal audit. Stay updated on industry codes and standards (AISC) and help ensure welding processes adhere to these specifications. Support adherence to safety protocols and practices during welding operations. Stay current with certifications and pursue additional training as necessary to maintain CWI status. Share guidance and training with welding personnel when needed. Work with the team to investigate and analyze welding-related issues, identify root causes, and recommend corrective actions to address deficiencies. Attention to detail.
cond_0459.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Current Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification
AWS D1.1 Credentials
Minimum of 2 years of experience in welding inspection within the steel fabrication and metal railings industry
Knowledge of welding inspection and related NDE methods (MT, PT, UT, and RT), including ASME Sec. V requirements
Proficient working knowledge and understanding of welding processes, including SMAW, GMAW, GTAW, and FCAW
Familiarity with welding codes and standards such as AWS, ASME, and API
Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with internal departments, suppliers, subcontractors, and regulatory authorities
Good verbal and written communication skills, including knowledge of AWS A3.0 Welding Terms and Definitions
Strong coordination and organization skills, with strict emphasis on accuracy and attention to detail
Must pass a drug test and background check
Clean driving record
Preferred Requirements
TxDOT industry experience
Understanding of specifications relevant to TxDOT requirements
Experience with AISC certification
Familiarity with coatings for steel — galvanized, painting, powder coating
Ability to analyze complex welding-related issues and fixture design challenges
Proven ability to analyze problems and implement effective solutions
Ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams

The CWI role is critical to the safety and structural soundness of buildings, vehicles, machinery, and consumer products that require strong, secure welds.
cond_0492.responsibilities:
Read plans and write reports complying with code specs. Communicate findings clearly with the quality control team and other departments on a regular basis.
Ensure that all materials specified on shop drawings and TxDOT form 1818 are used during fabrication and that accurate traceability of material through fabrication is maintained.
Ensure use of proper WPSs and properly certified welding personnel.
Perform visual inspection on welded products, structures in progress, and systems to assess quality, workmanship, and compliance with relevant codes, standards, and specifications.
Perform inspections both in-house and at vendor locations as needed, staying in regular contact with vendors and internal teams throughout the process.
Maintain accurate records of inspection activities, including reports on weld quality, non-conformities, and corrective actions. Ensure all documentation complies with relevant regulations.
Prepare detailed inspection reports, including photographs, drawings, and other relevant documentation as needed.
Collaborate daily with the quality control team to ensure welding procedures are followed and fabricated products meet required quality standards.
Verify proper weld joint preparation, fit-up, and evaluation of welds to the requirements of AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code - Steel or AWS D1.2 Structural Welding Code - Aluminum.
Use WPS or PQR sample forms located in the current applicable AWS code or approved equal.
Verify that repairs are made using the required repair procedure and that any required NDT is completed on the repair.
Conduct and stamp final acceptance of the product.
Actively contribute to the coordination of the annual AISC internal audit, connecting with relevant teams to keep the process on track.
Stay updated on industry codes and standards (AISC) and ensure welding processes adhere to these specifications.
Ensure adherence to safety protocols and practices during welding operations.
Stay current with certifications and pursue additional training as necessary to maintain Certified Welding Inspector status.
Provide guidance and training to welding personnel when needed, initiating discussions to address questions or issues as they arise.
Investigate and analyze welding-related issues, identify root causes, and recommend corrective actions to address any deficiencies. Communicate findings and recommendations clearly to relevant stakeholders.
Attention to detail.
cond_0492.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Current Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification.
AWS D1.1 Credentials.
Minimum of 2 years of experience in welding inspection within the steel fabrication and metal railings industry.
Knowledge of welding inspection and related NDE methods (MT, PT, UT, and RT), including ASME Sec. V requirements.
Proficient working knowledge (welder) and understanding of welding processes, including SMAW, GMAW, GTAW, and FCAW.
Familiarity with welding codes and standards such as AWS, ASME, and API.
Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with internal departments, suppliers, subcontractors, and regulatory authorities on a regular basis.
Good verbal and written communication skills, including knowledge of AWS A3.0 Welding Terms and Definitions.
Strong coordination and organization skills, with strict emphasis on accuracy and attention to detail.
Meticulous attention to detail in inspections and documentation.
Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.
Must pass a drug test and background check.
Clean driving record.
Must be able to read a tape measure.
Able to lift 50+ pounds.
Preferred Requirements
TxDOT industry experience.
Understanding of specifications relevant to TxDOT requirements.
Experience with AISC certification.
Familiarity with coatings for steel — galvanized, painting, powder coating.
Proven ability to analyze problems and implement effective solutions.

We are seeking an AWS Certified Weld Inspector (CWI) to support our structural steel fabrication and highway component/railings division. Certified Welding Inspectors employ their extensive knowledge of welding processes, test methods, discontinuities, materials, qualifications, and standards to ensure that weldments and welding-related activities comply with all applicable quality and safety criteria.
The role of the CWI is critical to the safety and structural soundness of the vast number of buildings, vehicles, machinery, and consumer products that require strong, secure welds. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of welding codes, inspection standards, and fabrication requirements.
cond_0535.responsibilities:
Able to read plans and write reports complying with code specs. Ensure that all Materials specified on the shop drawings and TxDOT form 1818 are used during fabrication and accurate traceability of the material through fabrication. Ensure use of proper WPSs and properly certified welding personnel. Perform Visual inspection on welded products, structures in progress, and systems to assess their quality, workmanship, and compliance with relevant codes, standards, and specifications. Performs inspections both in house and at vendor locations as needed. Maintain accurate records of inspection activities, including reports on weld quality, non-conformities, and corrective actions. Ensure all documentation complies with relevant regulations. Prepare detailed inspection reports, including photographs, drawings, and other relevant documentation as needed. Collaborate with the quality control team to ensure welding procedures are followed and fabricated products meet required quality standards. CWI verifies proper weld joint preparation, fit up, and evaluation of the welds to the requirements of AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code - Steel or the AWS D1.2 Structural Welding Code - Aluminum. Use WPS or PQR sample forms located in the current applicable AWS code or approved equal. Verification that repairs are made using the required repair procedure and any required NDT is completed on the repair. Final acceptance of the product is conducted and stamped by the CWI. Assist with the coordination of the annual AISC internal audit. Stay updated on industry codes and standards (AISC) and ensure welding processes adhere to these specifications. Ensure adherence to safety protocols and practices during welding operations. Stay current with certifications and pursue additional training as necessary to maintain Certified Welding Inspector status. Provide guidance and training to welding personnel when needed. Investigate and analyze welding-related issues, identify root causes, and recommend corrective actions to address any deficiencies. Attention to details.
Key Competencies:
MUST BE ABLE TO READ A TAPE MEASURE. Comply with Health and Safety, Environmental and company's manufacturing policies, and procedures. Maintains positive work atmosphere by functioning and communicating in an effective manner with co-workers, clients, quality control, and supervisors. Performs daily cleaning and maintenance of area. Works in a safe and conscientious manner. Lift 50+ pounds.
cond_0535.requirements:
Current Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification is required. Must have AWS D1.1 Credentials. Minimum of 2 years of experience in welding inspection within the steel fabrication and metal railings industry. TxDOT industry a plus. Understanding of specifications relevant to TXDOT requirements. Experience with AISC certification. Familiar with coatings for steel - galvanized, painting, powder coating. Ability to communicate effectively, both verbal and written, with all internal organization departments, suppliers, subcontractors, and regulatory authorities. Strong coordination and organization skills, with strict emphasis on accuracy and attention to detail. Good verbal and written communication skills, including knowledge of AWS A3.0 Welding Terms and Definitions. Knowledge of welding inspection and related NDE methods (MT, PT, UT, and RT), including ASME Sec. V requirements. Proficient working knowledge (welder) and understanding of welding processes, including SMAW, GMAW, GTAW, and FCAW. Familiarity with welding codes and standards such as AWS, ASME, and API. Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to analyze complex welding-related issues and fixture design challenges. Meticulous attention to detail in inspections and documentation. Proven ability to analyze problems and implement effective solutions. Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams. Must pass a drug test and background check. Clean driving records.
This Job Is Ideal For Someone Who Is:
Dependable -- more reliable than spontaneous. Adaptable/flexible -- enjoys doing work that requires frequent shifts in direction. Achievement-oriented -- enjoys taking on challenges, even if they might fail. Autonomous/Independent -- enjoys working with little direction. High stress tolerance -- thrives in a high-pressure environment.

We are seeking an AWS Certified Weld Inspector (CWI) to support our structural steel fabrication and highway component/railings division. Certified Welding Inspectors employ their extensive knowledge of welding processes, test methods, discontinuities, materials, qualifications, and standards to ensure that weldments and welding-related activities comply with all applicable quality and safety criteria.
The role of the CWI is critical to the safety and structural soundness of the vast number of buildings, vehicles, machinery, and consumer products that require strong, secure welds. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of welding codes, inspection standards, and fabrication requirements.
cond_0571.responsibilities:
Able to read plans and write reports complying with code specs. Ensure that all Materials specified on the shop drawings and TxDOT form 1818 are used during fabrication and accurate traceability of the material through fabrication. Ensure use of proper WPSs and properly certified welding personnel. Perform Visual inspection on welded products, structures in progress, and systems to assess their quality, workmanship, and compliance with relevant codes, standards, and specifications. Performs inspections both in house and at vendor locations as needed. Maintain accurate records of inspection activities, including reports on weld quality, non-conformities, and corrective actions. Ensure all documentation complies with relevant regulations. Prepare detailed inspection reports, including photographs, drawings, and other relevant documentation as needed. Collaborate with the quality control team to ensure welding procedures are followed and fabricated products meet required quality standards. CWI verifies proper weld joint preparation, fit up, and evaluation of the welds to the requirements of AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code - Steel or the AWS D1.2 Structural Welding Code - Aluminum. Use WPS or PQR sample forms located in the current applicable AWS code or approved equal. Verification that repairs are made using the required repair procedure and any required NDT is completed on the repair. Final acceptance of the product is conducted and stamped by the CWI. Assist with the coordination of the annual AISC internal audit. Stay updated on industry codes and standards (AISC) and ensure welding processes adhere to these specifications. Ensure adherence to safety protocols and practices during welding operations. Stay current with certifications and pursue additional training as necessary to maintain Certified Welding Inspector status. Provide guidance and training to welding personnel when needed. Investigate and analyze welding-related issues, identify root causes, and recommend corrective actions to address any deficiencies. Attention to details.
Key Competencies:
MUST BE ABLE TO READ A TAPE MEASURE. Comply with Health and Safety, Environmental and company's manufacturing policies, and procedures. Maintains positive work atmosphere by functioning and communicating in an effective manner with co-workers, clients, quality control, and supervisors. Performs daily cleaning and maintenance of area. Works in a safe and conscientious manner. Lift 50+ pounds.
cond_0571.requirements:
Current Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification is required. Must have AWS D1.1 Credentials. Minimum of 2 years of experience in welding inspection within the steel fabrication and metal railings industry. TxDOT industry a plus. Understanding of specifications relevant to TXDOT requirements. Experience with AISC certification. Familiar with coatings for steel - galvanized, painting, powder coating. Ability to communicate effectively, both verbal and written, with all internal organization departments, suppliers, subcontractors, and regulatory authorities. Strong coordination and organization skills, with strict emphasis on accuracy and attention to detail. Good verbal and written communication skills, including knowledge of AWS A3.0 Welding Terms and Definitions. Knowledge of welding inspection and related NDE methods (MT, PT, UT, and RT), including ASME Sec. V requirements. Proficient working knowledge (welder) and understanding of welding processes, including SMAW, GMAW, GTAW, and FCAW. Familiarity with welding codes and standards such as AWS, ASME, and API. Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to analyze complex welding-related issues and fixture design challenges. Meticulous attention to detail in inspections and documentation. Proven ability to analyze problems and implement effective solutions. Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams. Must pass a drug test and background check. Clean driving records.
This Job Is Ideal For Someone Who Is:
Dependable -- more reliable than spontaneous. Adaptable/flexible -- enjoys doing work that requires frequent shifts in direction. Achievement-oriented -- enjoys taking on challenges, even if they might fail. Autonomous/Independent -- enjoys working with little direction. High stress tolerance -- thrives in a high-pressure environment.

cond_0620.intro:
We are looking for an AWS Certified Weld Inspector (CWI) to join our structural steel fabrication and highway component/railings division.
Certified Welding Inspectors apply their knowledge of welding processes, test methods, discontinuities, materials, qualifications, and standards to ensure that weldments and welding-related activities comply with all applicable quality and safety criteria.
The CWI is critical to the safety and structural soundness of buildings, vehicles, machinery, and consumer products that require strong, secure welds.
cond_0620.responsibilities:
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to execute each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. This list is not all-inclusive.
Read plans and write reports complying with code specs.
Ensure all materials specified on shop drawings and TxDOT form 1818 are used during fabrication and maintain accurate material traceability through fabrication.
Ensure use of proper WPSs and properly certified welding personnel.
Execute visual inspections on welded products, structures in progress, and systems to assess quality, workmanship, and compliance with relevant codes, standards, and specifications.
Conduct inspections both in-house and at vendor locations as needed.
Maintain accurate records of inspection activities, including reports on weld quality, non-conformities, and corrective actions; ensure all documentation complies with relevant regulations.
Produce detailed inspection reports, including photographs, drawings, and other relevant documentation as needed.
Work with the quality control team to ensure welding procedures are followed and fabricated products meet required quality standards.
Verify proper weld joint preparation, fit-up, and evaluation of welds to the requirements of AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code - Steel or AWS D1.2 Structural Welding Code - Aluminum.
Use WPS or PQR sample forms located in the current applicable AWS code or approved equal.
Verify that repairs are made using the required repair procedure and that any required NDT is completed on the repair.
Conduct and stamp final acceptance of the product.
Lead coordination of the annual AISC internal audit.
Stay current on industry codes and standards (AISC) and ensure welding processes adhere to these specifications.
Enforce adherence to safety protocols and practices during welding operations.
Maintain certifications and pursue additional training as necessary to retain Certified Welding Inspector status.
Provide guidance and training to welding personnel when needed.
Investigate and analyze welding-related issues, determine root causes, and implement corrective actions to address deficiencies.
Maintain attention to detail throughout all tasks.

Proficient working knowledge (welder) and understanding of welding processes, including SMAW, GMAW, GTAW, and FCAW.
Familiarity with welding codes and standards such as AWS, ASME, and API.
Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with internal departments, suppliers, subcontractors, and regulatory authorities.

Working knowledge of specifications relevant to TxDOT requirements. Some experience with AISC certification is helpful. Familiarity with coatings for steel - galvanized, painting, powder coating. Ability to communicate effectively, both verbal and written, with all internal organization departments, suppliers, subcontractors, and regulatory authorities. Willingness to develop coordination and organization skills, with attention to accuracy and detail. cond_0643.intro:
We are seeking an AWS Certified Weld Inspector (CWI) to support our structural steel fabrication and highway component/railings division. Certified Welding Inspectors employ their extensive knowledge of welding processes, test methods, discontinuities, materials, qualifications, and standards to ensure that weldments and welding-related activities comply with all applicable quality and safety criteria.
The role of the CWI is critical to the safety and structural soundness of the vast number of buildings, vehicles, machinery, and consumer products that require strong, secure welds. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of welding codes, inspection standards, and fabrication requirements.
cond_0643.responsibilities:
Able to read plans and write reports complying with code specs. Ensure that all Materials specified on the shop drawings and TxDOT form 1818 are used during fabrication and accurate traceability of the material through fabrication. Ensure use of proper WPSs and properly certified welding personnel. Perform Visual inspection on welded products, structures in progress, and systems to assess their quality, workmanship, and compliance with relevant codes, standards, and specifications. Performs inspections both in house and at vendor locations as needed. Maintain accurate records of inspection activities, including reports on weld quality, non-conformities, and corrective actions. Ensure all documentation complies with relevant regulations. Prepare detailed inspection reports, including photographs, drawings, and other relevant documentation as needed. Collaborate with the quality control team to ensure welding procedures are followed and fabricated products meet required quality standards. CWI verifies proper weld joint preparation, fit up, and evaluation of the welds to the requirements of AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code - Steel or the AWS D1.2 Structural Welding Code - Aluminum. Use WPS or PQR sample forms located in the current applicable AWS code or approved equal. Verification that repairs are made using the required repair procedure and any required NDT is completed on the repair. Final acceptance of the product is conducted and stamped by the CWI. Assist with the coordination of the annual AISC internal audit. Stay updated on industry codes and standards (AISC) and ensure welding processes adhere to these specifications. Ensure adherence to safety protocols and practices during welding operations. Stay current with certifications and pursue additional training as necessary to maintain Certified Welding Inspector status. Provide guidance and training to welding personnel when needed. Investigate and analyze welding-related issues, identify root causes, and recommend corrective actions to address any deficiencies. Attention to details.
Key Competencies:
MUST BE ABLE TO READ A TAPE MEASURE. Comply with Health and Safety, Environmental and company's manufacturing policies, and procedures. Maintains positive work atmosphere by functioning and communicating in an effective manner with co-workers, clients, quality control, and supervisors. Performs daily cleaning and maintenance of area. Works in a safe and conscientious manner. Lift 50+ pounds.
